shape_hint: A headless double-ended threaded stud: full-form thread (B) on both ends, with a plain (or reduced/full-body) unthreaded shank in the middle; both ends chamfered/pointed; used with two heavy hex nuts for flange or bonnet joints.

role_map.B_le10: min nut-end full-thread length for stud length L<=10 in
role_map.Umax: max distance from end to first full-form thread (2 pitches, UNC)

notes: A193 Grade B6 / B6X is a 12% chromium martensitic stainless stud material (with A194 Gr 6 / 6F nuts); its dimensions come from the general stud standard ASME B18.31.2, so this table is the same as for any B18.31.2 double-end stud. Nut data (heavy hex, A194) are not included. Stud length is customer specified; both ends have the same B thread for clamping-type studs.

TorqBolt: torqbolt.com ASME B18.31.2 continuous-thread page (U min/max; Umax and D only)

verification.checks_done: Live re-download OK for a193gradeb7.com, boltingspecialist.com, nickel-systems, fasten.it, torqbolt (HTTP 200); aesteiron blocked by captcha -> producer copy parsed, not counted. Boltport pages a193gradeb7 and boltingspecialist: same 25-row table incl. 8UN dashes -> one cluster. Matrix 19 rows x 5 value columns (D, B_le10, B_10_16, B_gt16, Umax) x sources = 95 cells; 1 disagreement: Nickel prints D='0.1750' for 1-3/4 (typo; Boltport/TorqBolt 1.7500 and efunda/threadspec/fbc major dia 1.75 agree with the record). B columns: {Boltport, Nickel, fasten.it} = 3 clusters on rows 5/16, 3/8, 7/16, 1-1/8, 2-1/4, and on the other 14 rows too (+aesteiron, not counted). Umax (UNC): {Boltport, Nickel, TorqBolt} = 3 on all 19 rows (+aesteiron on 14). D: {Boltport, Nickel, TorqBolt} on 18 rows; 1-3/4 has Boltport + TorqBolt + (Nickel typo) -> confirmed by 3 other public pages (efunda, threadspec, fbc: 1.75). Physical: D = decimal of label on all rows; B_le10 < B_10_16 < B_gt16 by +0.25/+0.5; B_le10 monotonic 0.75..5.75; Umax = 2/tpi(UNC) 0.100..0.500.
problems: B and Umax columns are at exactly 3 clusters (Boltport, Nickel Systems, fasten.it / TorqBolt). Nickel's double-end table has the same headings ('Nut End Minimum Full Thread Length, Bmin', 'Umax = 2 Thread Pitches'), the same 25-row set and column grouping as Boltport's; typos differ (Nickel '0.1750', em-dash vs '--'), so it was counted as an independent transcription of the standard's table. If Nickel is judged a Boltport copy, the B columns drop to 2 clusters on all rows lacking aesteiron (5/16, 3/8, 7/16, 1-1/8, 2-1/4) and to 3 only by counting the unverifiable aesteiron elsewhere.

Nothing here is specific to A193 B6 / A194 Gr 6 (12Cr material specs only): this is the generic ASME B18.31.2 Table 2 (clamping-type double-end stud) and its B values equal the B columns of istud-te. Nut (A194 heavy hex) data are absent.
Boltport's own double-end page says 'Dimensions for Tap End Studs to ASME B18.31.2 Standard' (copy-paste slip) - table content nevertheless matches fasten.it 'table 2 clamping type studs'.
aesteiron.com cannot be re-fetched (captcha); its rows are scrambled, not used for the count.

Role check: B = 'Nut End Minimum Full Thread Length, Bmin' by stud length L (in), Umax = UNC column of 'Umax = 2 Thread Pitches', D = 'Diameter, D'; all read from headers. Sizes 3..4 in and 8UN-only sizes omitted (empty-cell rule).

standard_full: ASME B18.31.2 Table 2 (double-end / clamping-type studs), UNC series; A193 B6 / A194 Gr 6 are material specs only
